The HTTP API of `openvireo-sync-server`. It stores encrypted `.kdbx` files and never sees their contents.
See docs/api.md for how the pieces fit together.

Which routes exist depends on `SYNC_AUTH_MODE`: `standalone` has the database and pairing routes, `jwt` the
vault and internal routes, `both` all of them. `/health` and `/events` always exist. Routes the mode doesn't
have answer 404. The internal routes also need `SYNC_INTERNAL_TOKEN` to be set.

CORS: for origins in `SYNC_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` every route answers preflight with 204, allowing
`GET, HEAD, PUT, POST, DELETE` and the headers `Authorization, Content-Type, If-Match, If-None-Match`, and
responses expose `ETag, X-Database-Revision, Last-Modified`.

Every response has `Cache-Control: no-store`.

The machine-readable description is [openapi.yaml](/docs/sync-server/openapi.yaml) (OpenAPI 3.1.0); import it into an HTTP client or a code generator. [HTTP API](/docs/sync-server/api/) explains how the routes fit together.

### Authentication {#authentication}

| Scheme | |
|---|---|
| `device` | A device token (self-hosted). From `users add`, `devices add` or a pairing claim. |
| `access` | An account access token from the account server: EdDSA, `aud` containing `SYNC_AUTH_AUDIENCE` (default `ov-sync`), and a `vlt` claim mapping vault ids to `read`, `write` or `manage`. |
| `internal` | The `SYNC_INTERNAL_TOKEN` shared secret. |

### Databases {#databases}

A self-hosted user's databases, with device tokens

#### GET /api/v1/databases {#get-apiv1databases}

**List the user's databases** (`listDatabases`)

Token: `device`

| Status | |
|---|---|
| 200 | OK (object) |
| 401 | Missing, invalid or expired token (`Error`) |
| 403 | The token doesn't grant this, or is the wrong kind of token for the route (`Error`) |

#### GET /api/v1/databases/{id} {#get-apiv1databasesid}

**Download a database** (`getDatabase`)

HEAD works the same and returns no body.

Token: `device`

| Parameter | In | Type | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | path | string |  |
| `If-None-Match` (optional) | header | string | `*` on uploads (create only), an ETag on downloads (304 when unchanged) |

| Status | |
|---|---|
| 200 | The encrypted file (string (binary)) |
| 304 | The ETag in If-None-Match is still current |
| 401 | Missing, invalid or expired token (`Error`) |
| 404 | Not found (`Error`) |

#### PUT /api/v1/databases/{id} {#put-apiv1databasesid}

**Upload a database** (`putDatabase`)

`If-None-Match: *` creates it (412 if it exists). `If-Match: "<etag>"` replaces exactly that version (412
if another device uploaded in the meantime). With neither header the upload creates the database, or gets
428 if it already exists. Sends a `database` event to the user's other streams.

Token: `device`

| Parameter | In | Type | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | path | string |  |
| `If-Match` (optional) | header | string |  |
| `If-None-Match` (optional) | header | string | `*` on uploads (create only), an ETag on downloads (304 when unchanged) |

Request body (`application/octet-stream`): The encrypted database, starting with the KDBX file signature

| Status | |
|---|---|
| 200 | 200 when it replaced a version, 201 when it created the database or vault (`Meta`) |
| 201 | 200 when it replaced a version, 201 when it created the database or vault (`Meta`) |
| 400 | Invalid id, JSON or body (`Error`) |
| 401 | Missing, invalid or expired token (`Error`) |
| 412 | If-Match or If-None-Match didn't hold; download, merge and try again (`Error`) |
| 413 | Over SYNC_MAX_DB_BYTES; no body |
| 415 | The body isn't a KDBX file (`Error`) |
| 428 | The upload needs If-Match (update) or If-None-Match (create) (`Error`) |

### Devices {#devices}

Pairing new devices

#### POST /api/v1/devices/pairing {#post-apiv1devicespairing}

**Create a pairing code for another device of the same user** (`createPairingCode`)

Works once and for 10 minutes. A user has at most 5 codes waiting; a new one replaces the oldest.

Token: `device`

| Status | |
|---|---|
| 201 | Created (object) |
| 401 | Missing, invalid or expired token (`Error`) |

#### POST /api/v1/devices/pairing/claim {#post-apiv1devicespairingclaim}

**Trade a pairing code for a device token** (`claimPairingCode`)

Case, spaces and the dash in the code don't matter. Wrong codes are limited to 10 per client address and
100 in all per 10 minutes; after that, claims get 429 with Retry-After.

Token: none

Request body (`application/json`)

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | string |  |
| `deviceName` | string |  |

| Status | |
|---|---|
| 201 | The new device and its token, shown only once (object) |
| 400 | Invalid id, JSON or body (`Error`) |
| 429 | Too many wrong codes (`Error`) |

#### PUT /api/v1/vaults/{vault} {#put-apiv1vaultsvault}

**Create (manage) or update (write) a vault** (`putVault`)

`If-None-Match: *` creates it and needs the manage role. `If-Match: "<etag>"` updates it and needs write.
Without either header the upload always gets 428. Sends a `vault` event to the streams whose token lists
the vault.

### Events {#events}

Change notifications (server-sent events)

#### GET /api/v1/events {#get-apiv1events}

**Change notifications as server-sent events** (`streamEvents`)

Starts with `retry: 5000`; a `: ping` comment every 25 seconds keeps it open.

With a device token: `event: database`, data `{"id", "etag", "revision"}` or `{"id", "deleted": true}`,
for every change to one of the user's databases.

With an access token: `event: vault` (same data, for the vaults in the token) and `event: access`, data
`{"vault": uuid|null, "change": "granted"|"revoked"|"rotating"|"rotated"|"org"}`, when the account server
reports an access change for the token's subject. The stream ends once the token's `exp` has passed; the
client reconnects with a fresh token, and also after any `access` event.

Token: `device` or `access`

| Status | |
|---|---|
| 200 | The stream (string) |
| 401 | Missing, invalid or expired token (`Error`) |

### Internal {#internal}

Called by the account server only

#### POST /api/v1/internal/notify {#post-apiv1internalnotify}

**Push an access event to the open streams of some subjects** (`notifyAccess`)

Delivery is best effort. With Postgres, the event reaches streams on every instance.

Token: `internal`

Request body (`application/json`)

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `subjects` | array of `Principal` |  |
| `event` | `"access"` |  |
| `data` | object |  |

| Status | |
|---|---|
| 204 | Sent |
| 400 | Invalid id, JSON or body (`Error`) |
| 401 | Missing, invalid or expired token (`Error`) |

#### DELETE /api/v1/internal/vaults/{vault} {#delete-apiv1internalvaultsvault}

**Delete a vault and its history when no client does, e.g. an expired recovery archive** (`deleteVaultInternal`)

Token: `internal`

| Parameter | In | Type | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vault` | path | string (uuid) |  |

| Status | |
|---|---|
| 204 | Deleted; the vault's streams get a `vault` event with deleted true |
| 400 | Invalid id, JSON or body (`Error`) |
| 401 | Missing, invalid or expired token (`Error`) |
| 404 | Not found (`Error`) |

### Schemas {#schemas}

#### Meta {#meta}

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | The database id or vault UUID |
| `revision` | integer |  |
| `etag` | string | The quoted SHA-256 of the file |
| `size` | integer | Bytes |
| `updatedAt` | string (date-time) |  |

#### Principal {#principal}

string, matching `^(user|sa):[0-9a-f-]{36}$`

#### Error {#error}

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `error` | string | A message for people |
| `code` (optional) | `invalid_request`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`, `not_found`, `conflict`, `precondition_failed`, `precondition_required`, `rate_limited`, `internal_error` | Only on the vault and internal routes, and on /events when access tokens are accepted |
